theme: Xử lý xung đột trong nhóm

vocab.example: Most conflicts in my team started as a small misunderstanding.
vocab.example_vi: Phần lớn mâu thuẫn trong nhóm tôi bắt đầu từ một hiểu lầm nhỏ.

vocab.meaning_vi: buổi nói chuyện riêng giữa hai người
vocab.example: I asked him for a one-on-one because email made things worse.
vocab.example_vi: Tôi rủ anh ấy nói chuyện riêng vì trao đổi qua email làm mọi thứ tệ hơn.

vocab.example: We invited our manager to join as a neutral party for ten minutes.
vocab.example_vi: Chúng tôi mời quản lý tham gia mười phút với vai trò bên trung lập.

vocab.meaning_vi: tin rằng người kia có ý tốt
vocab.example: I try to assume good intent before I judge a colleague's message.
vocab.example_vi: Tôi cố tin rằng đồng nghiệp có ý tốt trước khi phán xét tin nhắn của họ.

vocab.meaning_vi: nghe ý kiến của cả hai bên
vocab.example: A good leader will hear both sides before making any decision.
vocab.example_vi: Một người lãnh đạo tốt sẽ nghe cả hai bên trước khi ra quyết định.

vocab.example: After twenty minutes we reached an agreement about urgent bugs.
vocab.example_vi: Sau hai mươi phút chúng tôi đạt được thoả thuận về cách xử lý lỗi khẩn cấp.

vocab.meaning_vi: làm dịu căng thẳng, nói ra cho rõ ràng
vocab.example: One honest conversation cleared the air between us completely.
vocab.example_vi: Một cuộc nói chuyện thẳng thắn đã hoàn toàn làm dịu căng thẳng giữa chúng tôi.

vocab.example: I try to stay objective and look at the facts, not personal feelings.
vocab.example_vi: Tôi cố giữ khách quan và nhìn vào sự việc, không nhìn vào cảm xúc cá nhân.

listening.title: Interview question: a conflict with a teammate

lines.speaker: Linh (HR Manager)
lines.text: Nam, can you tell me about a conflict you had with a teammate?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: Yes. Last year a tester and I disagreed about who should fix urgent bugs.

lines.speaker: Linh (HR Manager)
lines.text: That sounds stressful. What was the first thing you did?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: I asked him for a one-on-one coffee, because email was making things worse.

lines.speaker: Linh (HR Manager)
lines.text: And what did you learn in that conversation?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: It was mainly a misunderstanding. He thought I was ignoring his reports on purpose.

lines.speaker: Linh (HR Manager)
lines.text: How did you handle that moment?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: I tried to stay objective and hear both sides before suggesting any solution.

lines.speaker: Linh (HR Manager)
lines.text: Did you need help from your manager?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: Only once. We asked her to join as a neutral party for ten minutes.

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: We reached an agreement about urgent bugs, and that cleared the air completely.

questions.q: How did Nam start solving the problem?
options: He asked for a one-on-one coffee

questions.q: What role did the manager play?
options: She joined as a neutral party
She moved Nam to another team

shadowing: The situation was a disagreement about who should fix urgent bugs each week.
My task was to solve it quickly without hurting the team's daily work.
I invited him for a one-on-one coffee and let him speak first.
I tried to stay objective and hear both sides before suggesting a solution.
As a result, we reached an agreement and finished the release on time.
